name: Enterprise Workforce Landscape and Scope
constraints: Workforce Landscape is a reproducible projection and Workforce Scope is its versioned population and counting profile.
Neither construct creates a subject-model identity or writes to person, employment, assignment, position or organization masters.
Every published figure pins perimeter, world time, knowledge time, period convention, scope revision and source revisions.
Unique persons, legal headcount, distinct employed persons, active relationships, assignments, positions, FTE and capacity remain separately named measures.
Each measure declares its grain, denominator, time convention, inclusion predicate, source object, null policy, counting basis, consolidation and deduplication rules.

Person deduplication uses a transient engine-scoped anchor derived through WM-PER-001 identity resolution; it is non-registrable, never persisted or emitted, and never inferred from relationship multiplicity.
Employment, assignment and position identities remain distinct and active status is asserted rather than inferred.
Vacant positions contribute position or demand-side FTE measures but never create people.
Contractors, volunteers and agency workers may contribute assignments, allocated FTE or capacity without host legal headcount.

Dual employment creates multiple employment relationships but one person; assignment allocated supply FTE from WM-ORG-016 may exceed 1.0 across employers under a declared method and is never substituted for employment or demand FTE.
Unknown, suppressed and zero remain distinct states.
Scenario results remain separate from authoritative results.
WM-XCT-002 constrains purpose and audience while WM-XCT-003 fixes aggregate shape, suppression, grain and linkability.
Person anchors are resolved inside population calculation and never emitted in the released view.
Released views carry a reproducible fingerprint, provenance tuple, completeness state and suppression markers.
Workforce Scope is the versioned inclusion, counting, access and disclosure rule set; Workforce Landscape is the immutable result projected from one Scope revision and its pinned inputs.

A released view pins immutable revisions of WM-PER-001, WM-ORG-005, WM-ORG-016, WM-ORG-004, WM-ORG-002, WM-XCT-002 and WM-XCT-003 plus the calculation-engine revision; a missing required pin fails closed.

FTE measures name exactly one semantic class and source precedence: allocated supply FTE uses WM-ORG-016, authorized demand FTE uses WM-ORG-004, and an explicitly defined employment FTE may use WM-ORG-005; values from different classes are never coalesced or summed into one unnamed FTE.
Capacity names its class as person-available, assignment-available, position-authorized or unit-planned and never substitutes for headcount or FTE.

Employer legal headcount is the party-scoped count of qualifying WM-ORG-005 relationships for one legal employer; consolidated distinct employed persons is the anchor-deduplicated person count, and these canonical names are never aliased or collapsed.
Disclosure rules name cohort thresholds, suppression or aggregation action, release-set linkability and treatment of small counts, deltas, cross-tabs, unusual FTE and unique affiliation patterns.
Scope and Landscape identifiers are non-registrable artifact identifiers usable for citation and replay only, never as person, party, employment, assignment, position or organization keys.

Published profile revisions and view artifacts are immutable; changing a scope rule, source pin, access revision, disclosure shape or calculation-engine revision creates a new version and fingerprint.
Consolidated measures fail closed unless the pinned WM-XCT-002 access scope authorizes every contributing employer and source revision.
All measures combined in a cross-tab, delta or comparison share one declared release-level temporal convention or include an explicit reconciliation rule; otherwise the combined result is rejected.

Contractors, volunteers and agency workers enter unique persons only when a WM-PER-001 anchor resolves and the Scope inclusion predicate explicitly includes their assignment class; vacant positions never enter unique persons.
holds: WM-ORG-005 and WM-ORG-016 remain non-canonical and their composition relation is unapproved.
No shared normative FTE or headcount definition and no verified crosswalk exist.
Workforce measurement remains a gap in WM-ORG-016 and extension-grade in WM-ORG-002.
Privacy thresholds and cohort-control policy remain external, must be pinned and require canonical validation.
Canonical source fixtures and normative FTE/headcount crosswalk fixtures remain incomplete.
One frozen static audit is required before this checkpoint can be considered provider-reconciled.
